verdicts.reasoning: The diff does not use a design-system dialog component. The confirmation step is a hand-built div with role="alertdialog" that renders an inline Alert (intent="warning") in the section, so it is an inline warning rather than an overlay dialog. The API reference lists no dialog component, so the diff cannot be shown to use the DS confirmation pattern, and nothing in it confirms that one exists.

Neither confirm button has autoFocus, so nothing is default-focused, and the Cancel button is variant="secondary". The destructive styling is distinct. However, the confirm button is the destructive variant while Cancel is secondary, so the destructive action is arguably the most visually prominent action in the step, which fails the 'not visually primary' part. The diff also never moves focus into the alertdialog after it opens, so the focus behaviour is unverified. Ambiguous, so not a pass.

A visible Cancel button (variant="secondary") returns the user to idle in one click, before any deletion call. The copy says plainly: 'This action is permanent. Your account and all of its data will be deleted and can't be recovered.' The idle screen also states 'This can't be undone.' Minor gaps: there is no Escape-key handling or focus management, but the back-out path is clear.

output.overallNotes: The change adds a two-step delete flow: an idle warning, then an inline alertdialog with Cancel and a destructive confirm. Its strengths are the plain permanent-consequence copy and an easy Cancel path. It does not clearly meet the confirmation-pattern item, since it uses an inline Alert inside a hand-rolled alertdialog instead of a design-system dialog. The destructive-emphasis item is ambiguous because the destructive confirm button is arguably the visually dominant action in the step. Focus is never moved into the alertdialog, which weakens the accessible confirmation step, and the real deletion call is still a placeholder comment.
